Schon kleine Lichtquellen können deinem Körper signalisieren, dass es noch nicht Zeit zum Schlafen ist.

👉 Dunkelheit unterstützt die natürliche Produktion des Schlafhormons Melatonin.

✔ Vorhänge schließen

snippet.title: You NEED to Try This Galician Seafood in Madrid
snippet.description:
Dive into the raw, buzzing energy of Cervecería El Doble, an authentic Madrid institution that serves up some of the finest seafood in the city. This local favorite delivers a masterclass in simplicity, letting ultra-fresh ingredients take center stage. The seafood feast kicks off with exceptionally soft and tender Camarones from Galicia that will make you rethink regular shrimp forever, alongside unique Cañaíllas (sea snails) boiled to non-chewy perfection. The star power keeps climbing with delicate, butter-and-lime-laced Zamburiñas (mini scallops) unique to Spain, and sweet, intensely fresh Gambas Rojas. It’s a beautifully vibrant, no-frills experience that shows exactly why Madrid's seafood spots compete with the coast.

Embark on the ultimate Bangkok food tour with host Caro Santos-Neves as she journeys through the vibrant, high-heat world of authentic Thai cuisine. This comprehensive food guide maps out exactly where to eat in Bangkok, navigating everything from bustling local markets to historic kitchens and spice-packed street stalls. Teaming up with local food insiders and visionary chefs, Caro dives into a stunning cross-section of regional specialties, including comforting bowls of tofu nway, old-school wide rice noodles fried in rich pork fat, and adventurously bold Northern Thai relishes like nam prik ong. VIDEO INTRODUCTION:
The FIFA World Cup 2026 is happening right now. 32 nations are battling on the world's biggest football stage. And India? India is nowhere to be found. But here's what makes this even more painful. In 2019, Nita Ambani stood in front of 1.4 billion Indians and made a bold promise — that by the FIFA 2026 World Cup, India would be playing. Seven years later, we are not just missing from the World Cup. We are losing to Bangladesh. Our own players are recording videos begging FIFA to save Indian football. The headlines call it a funding problem. The news anchors call it a talent problem. But here's the thing nobody is telling you. India already spent over ₹5000 crore on football. Reliance, through a company called FSDL, alone pumped ₹4500 crore into a single league. Clubs paid another ₹777 crore in franchise fees just to participate. Broadcasters added ₹538 crore. Hero shelled out ₹160 crore in title sponsorship. So money is NOT the problem.
And here's the part that should make every Indian stop scrolling. Most Indians today have no idea that India was once the greatest football team in all of Asia. We were the inaugural Asian Games football champions in front of a packed crowd at the National Stadium in Delhi. We were the first Asian team to make the semi-finals at the Olympics in 1956. And we were so good that the Brazilian football team — yes, the Brazil — used to learn tactics from us. The world gave India a name we have all forgotten. They called us the "Brazil of Asia." On 4th September 1962, a hundred thousand people inside an Indonesian stadium booed every Indian pass, threw rocks at our team bus, and made one of our own players hide on the floor of the team bus just to avoid being hit. And in that ocean of hatred, the only people who cheered for India were the Pakistani hockey team. India still walked out of that stadium as Asian champions. That is who we used to be.
So how the hell did the country that taught BRAZIL football become the country that is losing to BANGLADESH? So in this case study, I want to answer three questions that no Indian media company is asking. How did India fall this far — from being the "Brazil of Asia" to losing to Bangladesh, despite spending over ₹5000 crore? How did the United Kingdom build a £15 billion football empire out of a system India refuses to copy? And most importantly, what is the ONE strategy India can steal from the UK to finally make Nita Ambani's FIFA World Cup dream real before it's too late?

snippet.title: Die dunklen Katakomben von Paris – Was dort lauert
snippet.description:
Tauche ein in die düstere und faszinierende Welt der Katakomben unter Paris! 🌑 In dieser spannenden Doku erkunden wir, was sich tief in den geheimnisvollen Gängen der Stadt der Liebe verbirgt.

👉 Von der Entstehung dieser unterirdischen Gräberstätte im 18. Jahrhundert, über die Millionen von Knochen, die hier lagern, bis hin zu den verbotenen Zonen, die nur die mutigsten Urbex-Abenteurer betreten – wir nehmen dich mit auf eine atemberaubende Reise unter die Oberfläche von Paris.

💀 Entdecke Mythen, Legenden und unheimliche Geschichten, die in der Dunkelheit der Katakomben weiterleben. Erfahre, welche Geheimnisse die endlosen Tunnel und die stummen Knochenwände erzählen – und warum sich bis heute Menschen in diesen verbotenen Gängen verirren.

📽️ Wenn dir dieses Video gefällt, vergiss nicht, es zu liken, zu abonnieren und mit deinen Freunden zu teilen!
